question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic boolean `memorySearch.queryInstructionTemplate` through public config and plugin embedding contracts, or keep model-specific preprocessing in provider-owned configuration or hooks?
rationale: Either design can support the proven behavior, but it establishes a lasting user and plugin API boundary that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Provider-Owned Preprocessing
options.body: Keep model-specific query and document transforms in provider-owned configuration or hooks rather than adding a generic boolean contract.

options.title: Approve Generic Boolean
options.body: Accept `queryInstructionTemplate` as public memory and plugin API after correcting Nomic and proving index upgrade behavior.

options.title: Narrow Initial Change
options.body: Ship only contract-correct query-only families through a smaller internal seam and defer API generalization.

recommendation.title: Provider-Owned Preprocessing
recommendation.body: Keep model-specific query and document transforms in provider-owned configuration or hooks rather than adding a generic boolean contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the provider-plugin embedding architecture and is the strongest history-backed owner for its public boundary.
